> لَقَدْ هَتَفَتْ فِي جُنْحِ لَيْلٍ حَمَامَةٌ * على فننٍ وهناً، وإنّي لنائم
> كذبتُ، وبيتِ الله، لو كنتُ عاشقاً * لَمَّا سَبَقَتْنِي بِالْبُكَاءِ الْحَمَائِمُ
> سَهَرُ الْعُيُونِ لِغَيْرِ وَجْهِكَ ضَائِعٌ
>
> "In the dark of night a dove cried out upon a swaying branch, while I lay fast asleep."

//: The book's own folder. Three things about a quotation are recorded there and not in the markdown — which Arabic the mushaf carries, which card a person declared for the rest, and each verse's citation — and the printed edition passes all three. The verse block is ayyuhal-walad's own, and it is THREE LINES on purpose: the renderers join a quotation's lines into paragraphs, so a multi-line poem is where the declaration used to be looked up under a string nobody wrote. Its third line deliberately carries no hemistich separator, which pins the whole-width line beside the split ones.
